hero.oneLiner: The deck positions Repco Home Finance as a Chennai-headquartered, NHB-registered housing finance company built on "relatively under-penetrated markets", a 100% retail book skewed to self-employed/non-salaried borrowers, direct customer contact and low-cost operations, with a heavily Tamil Nadu-weighted branch footprint.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "Repco Home Finance Ltd (RHFL) is a professionally managed housing finance company head quartered in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. We were incorporated in April 2000. We are registered as a Housing Finance Company (HFC) with the National Housing Bank (NHB)".
- Stated salient and unique features: "innovative loan products, direct customer contact and customer ownership, focus on quality customer servicing, transparency and speed of operations, focus on relatively under-penetrated markets and balanced portfolio mix, robust risk management systems and processes, low cost operations, established track record, stable and experienced senior management team".
- "100% of the loans given by the Company are retail loans" — no wholesale/developer exposure disclosed.
- Growth model described as "increasing our geographical footprint by deepening our reach selectively in existing regions and expanding to new regions".
- Loan book concentrated in Tamil Nadu at 57.3% of exposure (Jun-26), followed by Karnataka 11.4% and Maharashtra 9.8%; the deck highlights "Presence beyond South: branches in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, West Bengal, Odisha & Jharkhand".

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)
capital_allocation.body:
- Net Owned Fund of Rs 3,768 Crs (from Rs 3,401 Cr at Jun'25) with a Total Capital Adequacy Ratio of 36.1% — capital far in excess of regulatory need, and no deployment or return plan is disclosed.
- Total borrowings of Rs 12,078 Cr against a Rs 15,990 Cr book, with Commercial Banks the dominant source at Rs 10,474 Cr in Q1FY27 (up 13% YoY).
- ECL provision of 2.2% of the book (total ECL provision Rs 353 Cr), with Stage 3 coverage of 54.5% at Jun'26 — down from 64.7% at Jun'25 even as the Stage 3 pool fell from Rs 485 Cr to Rs 427 Cr.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Book vintage] The overdue breakup shows the legacy book carries the stress: of Rs 5,268 Cr sanctioned "Till March 2022", 5.8% (Rs 306 Cr) is Stage-3 and 13% (Rs 686 Cr) Stage-2, versus 1.1% (Rs 121 Cr) and 4.3% (Rs 466 Cr) respectively on the Rs 10,722 Cr book sanctioned "From April 2022" — post-2022 underwriting is materially cleaner.
- [Asset quality trend] GNPA improved to 2.67% at Jun-26 from 3.30% at Jun-25 (NNPA 1.23% vs 1.19%); Stage-2 assets are 7.2% of AUM at Jun'26 versus 9.7% at Jun'25, which the MD flags as "a marginal increase compared to previous quarter, while remaining improved compared to Q1FY 26".
- [Credit cost] Credit cost is shown running negative/near-zero in recent years — FY24 0.0%, FY25 -0.3%, FY26 -0.2%, FY27(3M) 0.2% — against 1.9% in FY22, i.e. recent earnings have benefited from provision write-backs rather than fresh provisioning.
- [Shareholding] Outstanding shares of 6.26 Cr; Promoters 37.1%, Mutual Funds 25.2%, Foreign Portfolio Investors 12.4%, Resident Individuals 19.0%; largest non-promoter holder is Bandhan Small Cap Fund at 9.8%.
- [Related-party funding] Repco Bank (associated with the promoter group by name) remains a lender at Rs 581 Cr and the highest average cost of any source at 8.50%, and is being run down (-36% YoY).
